lines.text: How long to walk to the Moon? Starting at your own front door.
lines.phonemes: hˌaʊ lˈɔŋ tə wˈɔːk tə ðə mˈuːn? stˈɑːɹɾɪŋ æt jʊɹ ˈoʊn fɹˈʌnt dˈɔːɹ.

lines.text: The Moon sits about thirty Earths away, lined up side by side, with nothing but dark between.
lines.phonemes: ðə mˈuːn sˈɪts ɐbˌaʊt θˈɜːɾi ˈɜːθs ɐwˈeɪ, lˈaɪnd ˌʌp sˈaɪd baɪ sˈaɪd, wɪð nˈʌθɪŋ bˌʌt dˈɑːɹk bᵻtwˈiːn.

lines.text: Walk at an easy pace, the kind you could chat through. Never stop, not even to sleep. You would arrive in about nine years.
lines.phonemes: wˈɔːk æɾ ɐn ˈiːzi pˈeɪs, ðə kˈaɪnd juː kʊd tʃˈæt θɹˈuː. nˈɛvɚ stˈɑːp, nˌɑːt ˈiːvən tə slˈiːp. juː wʊd ɚɹˈaɪv ɪn ɐbˌaʊt nˈaɪn jˈɪɹz.

lines.text: But nobody walks day and night. You sleep, you eat, you stop to tie a shoe. So give yourself a working day of walking.
lines.phonemes: bˌʌt nˈoʊbɑːdi wˈɔːks dˈeɪ ænd nˈaɪt. juː slˈiːp, juː ˈiːt, juː stˈɑːp tə tˈaɪ ɐ ʃˈuː. sˌoʊ ɡˈɪv jɔːɹsˈɛlf ɐ wˈɜːkɪŋ dˈeɪ ʌv wˈɔːkɪŋ.

lines.text: A working day of walking gets you there in about twenty-six years.
lines.phonemes: ɐ wˈɜːkɪŋ dˈeɪ ʌv wˈɔːkɪŋ ɡˈɛts juː ðɛɹ ɪn ɐbˌaʊt twˈɛntisˈɪks jˈɪɹz.

lines.text: Slower adds years, quicker trims a few. Ten thousand steps a day, the popular goal, is only about seven and a half kilometers. So that trip takes about a hundred and forty years.
lines.phonemes: slˈoʊɚɹ ˈædz jˈɪɹz, kwˈɪkɚ tɹˈɪmz ɐ fjˈuː. tˈɛn θˈaʊzənd stˈɛps ɐ dˈeɪ, ðə pˈɑːpjʊlɚ ɡˈoʊl, ɪz ˈoʊnli ɐbˌaʊt sˈɛvən ænd ɐ hˈæf kɪlˈɑːmɪɾɚz. sˌoʊ ðæt tɹˈɪp tˈeɪks ɐbˌaʊt ɐ hˈʌndɹɪd ænd fˈɔːɹɾi jˈɪɹz.

lines.text: Apollo eleven's crew made the same trip in about three days. The distance never changed, only the speed.
lines.phonemes: ɐpˈɑːloʊ ᵻlˈɛvənz kɹˈuː mˌeɪd ðə sˈeɪm tɹˈɪp ɪn ɐbˌaʊt θɹˈiː dˈeɪz. ðə dˈɪstəns nˈɛvɚ tʃˈeɪndʒd, ˈoʊnli ðə spˈiːd.

lines.text: Next envelope: what if everyone on Earth held hands?
